name: Website Design & Development
intro: Is your website helping people take the next step?

questions.text: How easy is it to complete your main action on a phone?
questions.action: Test your main call-to-action on a real phone.

questions.text: How well does your site explain what makes you different?
questions.action: Write a concrete promise for your best-fit customer.

questions.text: How reliable are your key pages, forms and links?
questions.action: Fix broken forms and navigation before redesigning.

questions.text: How easily can your team update important content?
questions.action: Choose an editing workflow your team can maintain.

questions.text: How well can you trace website inquiries to their source?
questions.action: Connect form and call conversions to useful reporting.

name: SEO & Search Visibility
intro: Find out whether organic search deserves closer attention.

questions.text: How easily do ideal customers find you for relevant searches?
questions.action: Validate non-branded visibility in your target market.

questions.text: How complete are pages for your key services and markets?
questions.action: Prioritize pages for services people actually want.

questions.text: When were crawling and indexing last checked?
questions.action: Check Search Console before buying more content.

questions.text: How well does organic traffic turn into useful inquiries?
questions.action: Review intent and conversion paths, not rankings alone.

questions.text: How consistently do you improve content using search data?
questions.action: Set a small, measurable search improvement backlog.

name: Paid Advertising
intro: Check for waste and missing foundations before scaling spend.

questions.text: How reliably are qualified leads or sales tracked?
questions.action: Validate conversions before increasing budget.

questions.text: How well do campaigns meet your cost-per-customer target?
questions.action: Set an affordable acquisition-cost target first.

questions.text: How closely do landing pages match the ads?
questions.action: Align one offer, one audience and one landing page.

questions.text: How regularly do you test and review campaign performance?
questions.action: Start with a controlled test, not unlimited scaling.

questions.text: How ready is your team to respond to new inquiries?
questions.action: Fix response and follow-up before paying for more leads.

name: AI Agents & Automation
intro: Find repeatable work worth improving, with human oversight.

questions.text: How much time goes to repeatable inquiries or admin each week?
questions.action: Measure task volume before automating.

questions.text: How often do slow replies or manual handoffs hold up customers?
questions.action: Choose one delay with a measurable customer impact.

questions.text: How standardized are answers and workflow rules?
questions.action: Document a narrow workflow before building an agent.

questions.text: Can the tools and information involved be connected safely?
questions.action: Review data access and integrations before deployment.

questions.text: Who would review exceptions and monitor quality?
questions.action: Assign a human owner and escalation rules.

gate: A high fit score is not approval to automate sensitive decisions. Low readiness in the last three answers calls for a preparation step, not an immediate agent rollout.

name: Email Marketing
intro: Look for useful lifecycle opportunities, not just more sends.

questions.text: How consistently do new subscribers or customers receive a welcome sequence?
questions.action: Design a welcome flow around the next useful action.

questions.text: How relevant are messages to each customer group?
questions.action: Start with a small number of meaningful customer groups.

questions.text: How effectively do you reconnect with inactive customers?
questions.action: Plan respectful re-engagement and suppression rules.

questions.text: How well do you measure email-driven business outcomes?
questions.action: Connect campaign activity to real outcomes.

questions.text: How ready is your permission-based contact list?
questions.action: Confirm consent, unsubscribe handling and list hygiene first.

gate: The final answer is a readiness check, not a need score. Without a usable permission-based list, build that foundation before a campaign. Do not upload a purchased list.

name: Social Media Marketing
intro: Check whether your content supports a clear business goal.

questions.text: How consistently do you publish useful content?
questions.action: Choose a cadence your team can sustain.

questions.text: How tailored is your content to the audience and platform?
questions.action: Adapt the message and format for each channel.

questions.text: How clearly does your content show your expertise or proof?
questions.action: Build a library of credible examples and stories.

questions.text: How reliable is your response to relevant comments and messages?
questions.action: Assign response ownership before increasing reach.

questions.text: How well do you connect social activity to useful outcomes?
questions.action: Measure inquiries and next steps, not likes alone.

name: CRM & Lead Management
intro: See where leads lose momentum between first contact and follow-up.

questions.text: Where are inquiries and customer details kept?
questions.action: Unify essential lead records before adding tools.

questions.text: How often do follow-ups get missed?
questions.action: Create next-action reminders and ownership.

questions.text: How clear is ownership of each opportunity?
questions.action: Define one accountable owner for each lead.

questions.text: How visible is the current sales pipeline?
questions.action: Agree a few pipeline stages with exit criteria.

questions.text: How well can you identify which channels produce customers?
questions.action: Capture source through the full customer journey.

name: Go-to-Market Strategy
intro: Check the assumptions behind your next growth move.

questions.text: How specific is your ideal customer profile?
questions.action: Interview a focused customer segment.

questions.text: How clear is the problem and outcome your offer addresses?
questions.action: Test the promise before scaling production.

questions.text: How well is pricing supported by customer and margin evidence?
questions.action: Check willingness to pay alongside delivery economics.

questions.text: How confident are you about which channels work?
questions.action: Run small channel experiments before a big launch.

questions.text: How clear are launch ownership, milestones and success measures?
questions.action: Turn strategy into owners, milestones and stop/go rules.

name: Brand Identity
intro: Find the gaps between what you deliver and how you look.

questions.text: How consistent is your visual identity across touchpoints?
questions.action: Audit a few high-visibility customer touchpoints.

questions.text: How distinct is your brand from close competitors?
questions.action: Define the difference before changing the logo.

questions.text: How well does your current identity fit your desired audience?
questions.action: Validate direction with the audience you want to serve.

questions.text: How easy is it for your team to make on-brand materials?
questions.action: Create a practical mini brand kit and templates.

questions.text: How well do brand assets work across mobile, print and social?
questions.action: Deliver accessible, scalable and reusable formats.
